Based on the provided onboarding document, there is no specific information or documentation regarding Gemma compatibility adapters, vLLM text-tool-call parsing, or handling raw `<|tool_call>` text tokens.

### Best Guess / Assessment
* **The Root Cause:** Hermes Agent expects standard OpenAI-compatible structured tool calls (i.e., structured `tool_calls` objects in the API response) to trigger its tool execution dispatcher. When serving models like Gemma via vLLM, the model outputs tool calls as inline raw text tokens (e.g., `<|tool_call>...<tool_call|>`) inside the content string while leaving `tool_calls: []` empty. 
* **The Fix:** Because Hermes does not natively recognize Gemma's raw text syntax out of the box, an adapter/normalization layer is required on the incoming stream and completion payload. This layer parses the raw `<|tool_call>` delimiters and converts them into structured OpenAI-style `tool_calls` dicts before handing them over to Hermes's dispatcher, while stripping any leaked special tokens (such as `<|channel>`) from the UI stream.
